projectDetails.name: Monero
projectDetails.description: Monero is a privacy-centric cryptocurrency that uses ring signatures, stealth addresses, and confidential transactions to provide fungible, untraceable payments.

topRisks.content: Missing CCSS certification leaves crypto custody controls unvalidated, increasing the risk of undetected security gaps.
The lack of a structured Bug Bounty program reduces proactive vulnerability discovery, raising the risk that attackers find issues first.

Several major exchanges (e.g., Huobi, Binance) intermittently restricted or delisted Monero trading or withdrawals citing compliance and traceability concerns, reflecting ongoing regulatory and monitoring risks rather than a protocol bug.

reviews.text: Monero is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency using ring signatures. Launched in 2014, it offers default anonymity. In 2025, it's still used for private transactions but often delisted due to regulations. Community-maintained development.

Monero is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency launched in 2014. It uses ring signatures, stealth addresses and bulletproofs to obscure senders, receivers, and amounts. Everyone in crypto knows Monero as the most private token. 100% of XMR supply is already mined (max around 18.4M XMR). Sometimes it is labelled as the dark money on the web that actually works, this because it is often used to blank malevolent transactions. Monero experienced an attempt of 51% attack by Qubic in mid-2025, that was able to manipulate 6 blocks, reducing its trust. The chain still maintains strong privacy properties.

Monero feels like the gold standard of privacy coins. Every time I use it, I have confidence that nobody can trace the payments. Its ring signatures and stealth addressing truly hide senders, receivers, and amounts. It’s built for folks who need anonymity. On the downside, this very feature draws regulatory heat agencies like the US Treasury have warned about Monero being used for illicit finance. That makes me a bit cautious, though I still respect it as the most private crypto we have.

Monero is a privacy focused cryptocurrency that aims to provide secure, untraceable transactions. Unlike Bitcoin and many other cryptocurrencies, Monero uses advanced cryptographic techniques such as ring signatures and stealth addresses to ensure that both the sender and receiver of a transaction are completely anonymous, as well as the transaction amount. This focus on privacy has made Monero the go-to cryptocurrency for those who prioritize confidentiality. However, its privacy features have raised concerns in some circles, especially regarding regulatory scrutiny.
